title: Tanzanian Fried Cassava Cakes
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Mikate ya Muhogo — grated cassava mixed with coconut milk, sugar, and cardamom, formed into small cakes and pan-fried until golden. A naturally gluten-free cassava breakfast cake sold at coastal morning markets.
longDesc: Cassava cakes are the gluten-free breakfast of the Tanzanian coast — grated fresh cassava combined with coconut milk and a little sugar produces small, golden, naturally sweet cakes that are completely satisfying in the morning.
steps: Grate cassava finely. Squeeze out as much moisture as possible through a cloth.
Combine grated cassava, coconut milk, sugar, cardamom, salt. Mix well.
The mixture should hold together when pressed — add more coconut milk if too dry.
Pan-fry in oil over medium heat 4—5 minutes per side until golden.
chefTips: Squeezing out moisture is essential — wet cassava produces a heavy, dense cake.
Press patties firmly — they must hold their shape.
commonMistakes: Patties that are too thick — raw inside.
cookingScience: Cassava contains linamarin which must be broken down — finely grating ruptures the cell walls, releasing linamarase enzyme which catalyses linamarin breakdown. The subsequent cooking completes the process. The starch in cassava gelatinises during pan-frying, binding the patty into a cohesive structure.
sustainabilityTips: Fresh cassava — Tanzania's most climate-resilient crop.
culturalNote: Cassava cakes are the coastal morning food of the practical Tanzanian cook — made from what grows locally, without any imported ingredients, producing a completely satisfying breakfast from the ground up.
